name: First Battle of the Marne
note: This plan shows the whole operation along a front of about 230 km, not a single field: each block is an army. The accounts give the armies' relative places (Paris in the west, Verdun in the east, the Aisne to the north) but no map of the lines, so the positions, the course of the rivers and the directions of the retreats are drawn by judgement. The Allied pursuit after 10 September is shown only in outline.

phases.title: The 6th Army meets the German right flank
phases.text: French reservists of the 6th Army, probing northeast of Paris, met the German IV Reserve Corps near the Ourcq. Though outnumbered, the corps attacked and held them for 24 hours before it retreated.
phases.quote: On 5 September, one day before Joffre's plan to begin the French offensive, the French and Germans clashed on Kluck's 1st Army's right flank.

phases.title: Kluck turns west and the 5th Army attacks Bülow
phases.text: Kluck turned his army to face west against the 6th Army and moved off its attacks. The right wing of the 5th Army attacked the German 2nd Army and pinned it, while the turn left a gap between the two German armies.
phases.quote: He ordered his army to turn to the right and face west to confront the threat from the French 6th Army.

phases.title: Bülow's right gives way while Hausen attacks Foch
phases.text: Bülow ordered his right wing to retreat while his left wing attacked with Hausen's 3rd Army. Hausen's night attack on Foch's 9th Army in the marshes pushed it back 13 km before it bogged down.
phases.quote: Hausen pushed Foch back 13 km (8.1 miles).

phases.title: The BEF and the 5th Army enter the gap
phases.text: The Allies sent the BEF northwest toward Kluck and the 5th Army northeast toward Bülow, into the gap between the two German armies. The BEF crossed the Petit Morin and established a bridgehead over the Marne.
phases.quote: The Allies exploited the gap in the German lines, sending the BEF northwest toward Kluck and the 5th Army northeast toward Bülow into the gap between the two German armies.

phases.title: Quast breaks through the 6th Army
phases.text: Kluck had telegraphed that an enveloping attack by General von Quast would bring the decision. Quast fought his way through the 6th Army's defences, and the way to Paris, 50 km away, lay open.
phases.quote: The next morning Quast fought his way through the defences of the French 6th Army and the way to Paris, 50 km (31 miles) distant, was open.

phases.title: Hentsch's order turns the 1st and 2nd Armies back
phases.text: Hentsch agreed with Bülow that a general retreat was needed once the Allies crossed the Marne. On 9 September Bülow withdrew again, and Kluck, with Bülow retreating, had no choice but to follow.
phases.quote: With Bülow retreating, Kluck had no choice but to follow suit.

phases.title: The Germans fall back to the Aisne
phases.text: Moltke ordered the 3rd, 4th and 5th Armies back as well, to the Aisne. The Germans retreated 65 km and dug in north of the river, pursued by the French and British at a slow pace.
phases.quote: The Germans were pursued by the French and British, although the pace of the exhausted Allied forces was slow and averaged only 19 km (12 mi) per day.
